title: csw-title
label: Tank

won.source: csw-title.html's own header: "CSW World Title (1/1996 - 8/1996)".

how: wins title in a battle royal by eliminating Mercury to become the 1st CSW World Champion
note: Corroborated from the champion's own side: Tank's own served bio reads "Tank was a rookie when he came too the csw and became the 1st world champion," and names the founding cast he won it out of — "Mercury, Miguel Sanchez, Machine of War, Powler, Austin 9:11, Facing Death, Ace Stevens, Billy Monroe, Loose Canon, Mr. Ravshings and a few others." The same bio places him, later and elsewhere, as the FIRST champion of JL Black's separate CSW 2 as well ("At the start of the CSW 2 he was there 1st champion again") — a different promotion, not a second reign on this belt.

won.source: No per-reign date survives on the fed's own numbered ledger — only the title's own creation and closing (acquisition) dates are recorded.

label: Heartbreaker

won.source: No per-reign date survives on the fed's own numbered ledger — only the title's own creation and closing (acquisition) dates are recorded.

note: SOURCES DISAGREE ON THE ORDINAL, recorded not resolved. This ledger numbers the Heartbreaker third, after Ace Stevens. His own served bio numbers him second and names a different man beaten for it: "Heartbreaker beat Tank for the CSW title. Heart became the 2nd man to be the CSW Champion. Heart would be champion for about a month's time when he lost it to Mr. Ravishing of the UBH" — and his own ex-wrestler story signs off "One day the 2nd CSW Champion will return." The ledger's own succession (Tank → Ace Stevens → Heartbreaker → Mr. Ravishing) agrees with the bio on who took the belt off him and disagrees on who he took it from. Neither is preferred here.

label: UBH (Miguel Sanchez & Zamza)

won.source: No per-reign date survives on the fed's own numbered ledger — only the title's own creation and closing (acquisition) dates are recorded.

how: wins titles at a house show, however titles stripped by the CSW and award back to the Raxton Brothers
note: SOURCES DISAGREE ON WHETHER THIS REIGN HAPPENED AT ALL, recorded not resolved. The ledger records it plainly ("wins titles at a house show, however titles stripped by the CSW and award back to the Raxton Brothers") and Zamza's own served card lists "CSW World Tag Team Champion" among his titles won — but the prose on that same page says the win never came: "Near the end of the CSW's life, Zamza and Sanchez became a tag team and were going to win the CSW World Tag Titles at the following PPV but the csw shut down that same month." One page, two accounts. Kept as the ledger records it, with the denial named here.
